per_question.question: What medical loss ratio (MLR) must Medicaid managed care organizations meet under federal law, and how does NC implement this requirement?
per_question.agent_answer:
Under federal law, Medicaid managed care plans must **calculate and report** an MLR, but a plan is not automatically subject to a federal minimum threshold unless the **state chooses to require one by contract**. If a state does require a minimum MLR, the minimum must be **at least 85%**. North Carolina’s implementation evidence I found shows NC assures its rates are designed to reasonably achieve an **85% MLR standard**, and in the NC SPA material retrieved, the State says it **does not require remittances** from MCOs, PIHPs, or PAHPs for failing to meet a minimum MLR. [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438); [SPA 22-0013 Proposed Amendments CHIP-Managed Care](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/22-0013-proposed-amendment-chip-managed-care/download?attachment)

## Federal rule

### 1) What federal law requires
Under **42 C.F.R. § 438.8(a)**, the state must ensure through its contracts that each MCO, PIHP, and PAHP **calculates and reports** an MLR in accordance with the regulation. That is the baseline federal requirement. [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

### 2) Is there a federally mandated minimum percentage?
Not by default. Under **42 C.F.R. § 438.8(c)**, **if a state elects to mandate a minimum MLR**, that minimum must be **equal to or higher than 85 percent**. So the federal rule is:

- **reporting/calculation is mandatory**, but
- a specific **minimum threshold is conditional on state election**, and
- if elected, it must be **at least 85%**. [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

### 3) How the federal MLR is calculated
Under **42 C.F.R. § 438.8(d)**, MLR is the ratio of the **numerator** to the **denominator**, with a possible **credibility adjustment** for partially credible plans. [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

At a high level, **42 C.F.R. § 438.8(e)** says the numerator includes:
- **incurred claims**,
- **expenditures for activities that improve health care quality**, and
- **fraud prevention activities**. [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

The same section also specifies adjustments, including that certain items must be deducted from incurred claims, such as:
- **overpayment recoveries from network providers**, and
- **prescription drug rebates received and accrued**. [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

The denominator rules are also set in **§ 438.8**, and the regulation permits a **credibility adjustment** under **§ 438.8(d)** and **(h)** for partially credible plans. I can confirm the rule requires those methodology components, but I did not retrieve the full denominator text in this turn, so I’m keeping that part at a high level. [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

### 4) Federal oversight and remittances
Under **42 C.F.R. § 438.74(a)**, the state must annually submit to CMS a summary of each MLR report received from its MCOs, PIHPs, and PAHPs. That summary must include at least:
- the numerator amount,
- the denominator amount,
- the MLR percentage,
- member months, and
- any remittances owed. [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

Under **§ 438.74(b)**, if the state requires remittances for failure to meet the state’s minimum MLR, the state must reimburse CMS for the federal share and submit a separate methodology report. [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)

## North Carolina implementation

The NC implementation evidence in the retrieved SPA section states that:

- the State assures its payment rates are designed to reasonably achieve a medical loss ratio standard **equal to at least 85 percent** for the rate year; and
- the State annually submits to CMS a summary description of the MLR reports it receives from MCOs, PIHPs, and PAHPs. [SPA 22-0013 Proposed Amendments CHIP-Managed Care](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/22-0013-proposed-amendment-chip-managed-care/download?attachment)

The same retrieved NC SPA text also states:

- **“No, the State does not require any MCO, PIHP, or PAHP to pay remittances.”** [SPA 22-0013 Proposed Amendments CHIP-Managed Care](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/22-0013-proposed-amendment-chip-managed-care/download?attachment)

## Bottom line

- **Federal law:** Plans must **calculate and report** MLR; a **minimum MLR is only required if the state elects one**, and then it must be **at least 85%**. [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438)
- **North Carolina:** The retrieved NC implementation text says rates are designed to reasonably achieve **at least 85%**, NC reports MLR information to CMS, and the retrieved SPA text says NC **does not require remittances** for not meeting a minimum MLR. [SPA 22-0013 Proposed Amendments CHIP-Managed Care](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/22-0013-proposed-amendment-chip-managed-care/download?attachment)

## Amendment status
I checked amendments for the federal regulation and the NC SPA document cited here. The tool returned **42 CFR Part 438** and **SPA 22-0013 Proposed Amendments CHIP-Managed Care** as the authoritative current documents, with no separate amendments returned for either in this corpus.

It correctly describes the numerator components (incurred claims, quality improvement activities, fraud prevention), mentions credibility adjustments, and covers reporting requirements and remittance rules. The NC implementation details are accurate - NC designs rates to achieve 85% MLR, reports to CMS, but does not require remittances. Citations are precise with specific CFR section references (438.8(a), (c), (d), (e), (f), (h), 438.74).
